errors.claim: The excluded methods listed in the thesis are all characterised as non-causal approaches.
searches: non-causal|do not focus on cause|focus on caus
path analysis|concept mapping|social network analysis|viable systems
errors.source_check: The source says it almost entirely ignores approaches not focused on cause and influence, but it does not classify every named excluded method as non-causal.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to other systems-mapping methods outside the book's selected causal and participatory scope

errors.claim: Figure 1.3 distinguishes purely visual, network-analysis, dynamic/simulation, and probabilistic output regions.
errors.source_check: The converted source retains only Figure 1.3's caption; the figure's internal labels are absent, and no matching prose names these four regions.
errors.suggested_fix: delete the four named regions unless verified from a complete source rendering

errors.claim: Table 1.2 contains the full enumerated list of nineteen excluded methods and schools reproduced in the reference.
searches: Table 1.2|methods not included|not in this book
errors.source_check: The converted source says Table 1.2 covers excluded methods, but the table body is absent. Some names occur separately in the index, references, or following prose; the complete list cannot be verified from the supplied source text.
errors.suggested_fix: delete the complete enumeration or restore and verify the missing Table 1.2 text

errors.claim: Two NHS-related Rich Pictures are presented: the UK NHS picture and the sustainable-development picture from Slovakia.
errors.source_check: Figure 2.1 concerns the UK NHS; Figure 2.2 concerns the influence of indicators on sustainable development in Slovakia and is not NHS-related.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to two Bell and Morse examples, one concerning the UK NHS and one concerning sustainable development in Slovakia

errors.claim: A Rich Pictures workshop typically runs from a thirty-minute minimum to two hours.
errors.source_check: The source says a workshop can run in as little as thirty minutes if needed but more commonly around two hours; it does not establish thirty minutes as a typical minimum.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to as little as thirty minutes if needed, but more commonly around two hours

errors.claim: Participatory Systems Mapping has nine basic stages.
searches: Deciding on aim|Analysis design|Verification and review
errors.source_check: The source enumerates ten stages: aim, system boundary, stakeholders, process design, focal factors, general factors, map building, factor/connection information, verification/review, and analysis design.

errors.claim: Positive PSM connections mean that factors 'move together mathematically'.
searches: positive means they move together|normative way
errors.source_check: The source says positive is used 'in a mathematical sense' and then says the factors 'move together'; the combined quotation 'move together mathematically' is absent.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to the verbatim phrase 'they move together' or change the marker to [AP]

errors.claim: The Bayesian-network history quotation says 'the field as it is recognized today was born'.
searches: field as it is recognised|field as it is recognized
errors.source_check: The supplied source uses UK spelling: 'the field as it is recognised today was born'.

errors.claim: Forrester used hand simulations to explore employment dynamics with General Electric managers.
errors.source_check: The source qualifies this historical account with 'Legend has it' and an editorial aside; the reference presents it as an unqualified fact.

errors.claim: National-scale data-rich systems are the most amenable to quantitative data-driven system mapping.
searches: one of the most appropriate|most amenable
errors.source_check: The source says systems defined at national or other data-rich scales 'may be one of the most appropriate' cases; it does not claim they are definitively the most amenable.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier may be among the most appropriate

errors.claim: Workshop facilitators should work in pairs but not in larger teams.
errors.source_check: The source says working in pairs can be useful and separately warns that facilitation can become muddled when perhaps four or five people are perceived as facilitators. It gives no hard maximum of two.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to working in pairs can be useful; avoid having four or five people perceived as facilitators

errors.claim: The first rung of the ladder of using methods is 'Maslow's hammer'.
errors.source_check: Maslow is absent. The source says only: 'You have your hammer, and now everything looks like a nail.' A similarly worded title appears in the Prell et al. bibliography, without attribution to Maslow.

errors.claim: The seven-method list in the statistics table is verbatim.
searches: seven systems mapping methods|in alphabetical order
Bayesian Belief Networks|Theory of Change maps
errors.source_check: The source introduces the methods alphabetically as BBN, CLD, FCM, PSM, Rich Pictures, System Dynamics, and Theory of Change. The reference reorders them into chapter order, so its list is a faithful paraphrase but not verbatim.

errors.claim: Rich Pictures workshops support up to twenty participants per facilitator.
searches: as many as twenty per facilitator|groups as large as fifty
three to six people|up to 20 participants
errors.source_check: The source says 'perhaps as many as twenty per facilitator', preserving uncertainty; 'up to twenty' turns that observation into a firm ceiling.
errors.suggested_fix: add qualifier perhaps as many as twenty per facilitator

errors.claim: Balancing loops are self-stabilising and reinforcing loops are runaway.
searches: reinforcing feedback loop|runaway change|carry on increasing
errors.source_check: The source says balancing loops tend to self-stabilise and reinforcing loops tend to carry on increasing or decreasing. The compact 'reinforcing, runaway' formulation is a paraphrase, not verbatim.
errors.suggested_fix: correct marker to [AP] or quote the source wording

errors.claim: The four FCM dynamic-analysis outcomes are verbatim as 'stabilise at new values; runaway change; return to zero; cycles'.
searches: four types of outputs|stabilise at new values
errors.source_check: The source gives four full clauses describing changes in factor values. The reference compresses them into accurate labels, which are paraphrased rather than verbatim.

errors.claim: Highly technical black-box modelling is criticised specifically because it does not lead to action.
errors.source_check: The source enumerates 'highly technical black-box modelling' separately from 'appealing metaphors and language which don't directly lead to action'. The reference transfers the latter qualifier to the first item.
errors.suggested_fix: correct to highly technical black-box modelling, without the does-not-lead-to-action qualifier

errors.claim: The authors frame against forcing all decisions through severity-of-outcome or canonical category boxes in Theory of Change diagrams.
searches: canonical categor|category boxes|narrow or overly simple
errors.source_check: absent. The source criticises pressures to produce narrow or overly simple ToCs, but it does not mention severity-of-outcome decision rules or canonical category boxes.

errors.claim: The authors explicitly name a 'Maslow's-hammer failure mode'.
errors.source_check: Maslow is never named. The source uses the unattributed sentence 'You have your hammer, and now everything looks like a nail.'
errors.suggested_fix: correct to hammer-and-nail failure mode and remove the Maslow attribution
